notes: Reads younger than the intended forties; curls are longer than the cropped brief. Bow is larger than the specified shortbow.
Spindle and stitch identity works. Broad build could be more pronounced; lantern and gold trim are more ornate than intended.
Clock focus reads clearly. Gold ornaments make practical watchmaker workwear more ceremonial than intended.

Scar and undercut read well. An unwanted arrow quiver was generated behind her shoulder; remove in a later agreed design revision. Blade is a fencing sword rather than the intended warblade; swept hair is longer than brief.
Reads younger than the intended fifties. Ringed focus became a fire-orb apparatus and the tome gained Pip-like leaf ornament instead of a ledger motif.
Conductor silhouette is clear. Numerous gold fittings make the work coat more ornate than the intended practical design.
Shaved head, broad nose and green palette distinguish him. Lantern is bright rather than hooded with a narrow slit.
Strong build, cream padding and red scarf fit the brief. Curls are more expansive than intended; oven-glass lantern identity is not clear.
Bob, triangular glass focus and cobalt colours work. Coat reads longer and more ceremonial than the practical brief.
Elderly face and muted blue fit. Shield is more substantial than intended; added hood broadens the silhouette.
Arch focus, testament motif and violet lantern work. Intended age of sixties remains understated.
Heavyset silhouette is less pronounced than intended. Braid is longer; lantern lacks clear frosted-glass identity.
Massive build and ochre palette fit well. Shield has more gold ornament than the plain equipment direction.
Muscular sleeveless silhouette works. Loose curls dominate instead of tightly braided hair; broken nose is not clearly conveyed.
Lanky build, sand coat and auburn hair fit. Sword is slender fencing gear; shield is more decorated than the plain brief.
Freckles and plum palette work. Tousled hair replaces the close crop; face reads younger than the intended adult.
Thickset older fighter and compact matching gauntlets are strong identity matches. Gloves are heavily padded.
Clipped hair, anatomical tome and split-circle staff fit. Staff is heavier and more luminous than the slender brief.
Heavy female silhouette and fixed poleaxe work. Poleaxe top nearly touches the board edge and needs more margin before a production master.
Older short, sturdy crossbow identity works well. Ammunition case reads more like an arrow quiver than a compact bolt case.
